summary.headline: TeamLease Q2 FY27 revenue rose 1% QoQ to INR3,086 crore and operating EBITDA rose 17% QoQ to INR44 crore, but associate headcount fell about 5,500 after a margin-dilutive exit.
summary.overview: Management described the quarter as a deliberate reset that fell short of its own aspirations. Revenue was flat-to-up at INR3,086 crore and operating EBITDA grew faster than revenue, helped by specialized staffing and the EdTech seasonal pickup. Reported EBITDA was INR36 crore (1.2% margin) and PBT of INR30 crore included non-recurring other income in Q1. Associate count closed near 2.85 lakh, down about 5,500, mainly due to the exit of one negative-margin client with over 7,000 associates, while BFSI declined. Management is pivoting to higher-margin verticals, portfolio pruning and an M&A framework, with net free cash of INR350 crore after the INR238 crore buyback.

segments.name: General staffing
segments.commentary: Associates closed at about 2.85 lakh, net down about 5,500; excluding a 7,000+ associate negative-margin exit, underlying net adds were about 1,500. Gross hiring about 62,500, highest in three quarters; 32 new logos, about 75% under variable or outcome-based pricing. Staffing PAPM stated at INR700.

segments.name: Specialized staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR190 crore; India EBITDA margin 7.6% and global 4.3%; GCCs about 69% of segment revenue; more than 135 GCC clients vs over 110 at FY-end. Core team about 2,790, up from about 2,500 in March; 7,670 associates across IT and specialized skills.

segments.name: HR services (EdTech, HR tech)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose QoQ on EdTech seasonality; segment EBITDA margin 3% per CEO, and management guided 5-6% margin ahead. Crystal HR 30% stake divested under put option at about INR10 crore, with no loss of principal.

segments.name: Global business
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 51% YoY; global operating margin 5% vs 3% in prior quarter after exiting low-margin mandates; more than 100 people outside India.

segments.name: Apprenticeship (within HR services)
segments.commentary: Management cited an average PAPM of about INR600 for the apprenticeship business, which was the source of the INR600 figure queried on the call.

guidance_outlook: General staffing: management expects double-digit YoY growth in absolute profit for general staffing and margin expansion via operating leverage, without quantifying basis points.
Specialized staffing: at least another 20 bps EBITDA margin improvement by Q4 FY27; no timeline given for 8-9% margin.
HR services: 15-20% revenue growth for the next one to two quarters, with 5-6% EBITDA margin.
Headcount: expects return to consistent net adds; Q3 has over 16,000 open positions; temporary festive headcount to normalise by year-end, FTE back to about 350.
Q3 furloughs already built into the annual plan; labour code and PF ceiling changes expected to be cost pass-through with no P&L impact on the associate book.
Operating EBITDA growth to come from earnings engine irrespective of volumes, per management.
capex_capacity: Technology: ground-up overhaul of associate lifecycle system; some elements live, more in Q3, full rollout expected in Q4 FY27.
Client and associate databases being integrated for on-demand commercial and workforce intelligence; AI and automation applied to process workflows.
Hiring technology cut cost per hire by about 30% in general staffing and about 40% in specialized staffing over 18 months; manufacturing hires cost about INR3,000 per hire, FMCG as low as INR1,000.
Own sourcing: about 19,000 joinees, 31% of gross joinees in Q2 vs 28% in Q1; management says average above 40% over recent quarters.
Capital priorities: technology, people, leadership in the core, then margin-accretive M&A in adjacencies; no advanced-stage deal disclosed.
demand_pricing: BFSI declined in aggregate on headcount due to reductions in a few large accounts, partly offset by wallet-share gains in private banks, small finance banks and mid-sized NBFCs.
Consumer (durables, retail, e-commerce led by quick commerce) grew strongly and offset BFSI.
Telecom: operators now prefer human deployment for field and customer-facing roles over automation; hiring ramped in several pockets.
IT services hiring cautious, mostly replacement; demand led by AI/ML, data engineering, cloud, DevOps, cybersecurity and SAP skills; over 800 AI professionals placed under ATLIS in H1.
Diwali fell about three weeks later than last year, so festive hiring arrived in clusters; September 30 headcount was measured between clusters.
Staffing PAPM marginally up per management (INR700); specialized staffing PAPM up about 10% YoY on higher-value AI and data hiring.
Global and GCC demand remains the main growth driver for specialized staffing.

qa_highlights.question: Has general staffing headcount bottomed, and can volume growth reach 5-6% steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify a growth percentage; it said the H2 plan is headcount addition, with more selective, profitable mandates. Softness was attributed to one-offs (about 35,000 associates lost over five quarters, including a 28,000 NBFC absorption under an RBI rule) and client tentativeness.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAPM falling to INR600 in general staffing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said staffing PAPM is about INR700 and rose marginally; the INR600 figure refers to the apprenticeship business. Specialized staffing PAPM rose about 10% on higher-value AI hiring.

qa_highlights.question: How is there no capital loss on the Crystal HR exit given INR25 crore investment and INR10 crore sale?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the 30% stake cost about INR10 crore and was recovered in full; the exit was taken while the call option was available to avoid buying the balance stake as SaaS businesses faced AI-related pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the loss-making HR business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is realigning the portfolio: adding new offerings and pruning verticals with weak demand; HR services guided to 15-20% growth and 5-6% EBITDA margin over the next one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: M&A size, timing and areas?
qa_highlights.answer: Framework still at an early stage; targets are either scale-up in existing businesses or adjacent entry into new talent-solution verticals, with a high-margin requirement above current weighted margin. No ticket size or timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is OCF negative in H1 and receivables up about 16%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to about INR120 crore of ad hoc one-day funding extended to clients around the EPFO wage ceiling change on September 17, recovered the next day; receivables were about INR630 crore vs INR540 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will specialized staffing margins reach 8-9%?
qa_highlights.answer: No exact guidance; gradual improvement expected with ATLIS, GCC focus and higher-margin profiles, with at least 20 bps more by Q4 FY27.

risks_watch: Continued headcount weakness in general staffing and BFSI account reductions; watch Q3 net adds against 16,000 open positions.
Labour Code and EPF wage ceiling changes: management expects pass-through, but associate take-home reduction creates retention risk.
Operating cash flow turned negative in H1 and receivables rose; watch whether the ad hoc funding reverses and DSO stays at 6 days.
Reported vs operating EBITDA gap from buyback and brand/tech investments; unallocated corporate cost at INR8 crore.
Portfolio pruning in HR services and possible M&A deployment of the INR350 crore net free cash.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the quarter, which management called short of its own aspirations and a deliberate reset. Confident on the medium-term engine (specialized staffing, GCCs, technology) but evasive on quantified headcount growth, margin trajectory and M&A timing, repeatedly deferring to qualitative commentary.
key_quotes: We recognize that this quarter's results fell short of our own aspirations and of the expectations of our stakeholders.
It is encouraging that our operating businesses are growing profit faster than revenue.
We may have to weed some of the non-aligned businesses, which allow bandwidth to seed new verticals.
Growth is very much on our agenda, and the growth will come from headcount, and we are totally focused on it.

growth.why: Guidance is narrow: general staffing double-digit absolute profit growth, specialized staffing at least +20 bps margin by Q4 FY27, and HR services 15-20% growth for one to two quarters, with 5-6% HR margin; no group revenue guidance, and backing is partial (32 new logos, GCC wins, own sourcing, a Q3 open-position pipeline of 16,000+) with no capacity additions quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Specialized staffing guided to at least +20 bps EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27 (India 7.6%, global 4.3%), and general staffing double-digit absolute profit growth is expected via operating leverage, though no basis-point figure was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches discussed; the spend is on technology (associate lifecycle system fully rolled out in Q4 FY27) and the company is pruning a negative-margin client and HR verticals, not adding physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Net associate count fell about 5,500 to roughly 2.85 lakh (about 1,500 underlying net adds ex the 7,000+ exit), with over 16,000 open Q3 positions and gross hiring of about 62,500 as the H2 plan, but management gave no quantified volume growth and BFSI declined.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed and no capacity additions are planned; capital priorities are technology, people and leadership with margin-accretive M&A only at framework stage and no advanced deal disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was narrowed and partly cut (HR services margin set at 5-6% vs prior aspirations, 8-9% specialized margin timing dropped) and management called the quarter short of its own aspirations.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Headcount is still net down, Q3 net adds must absorb 16,000+ open roles, and HR services margin of 3% in the quarter is well below the 5-6% guided range; a further miss on Q3 hiring or HR margin would force a cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said it is adding new HR services offerings and pruning weak verticals, and ATLIS placed over 800 AI professionals in H1, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Hiring tech cuts cost per hire
rows.why: Hiring technology is guided to cut cost per hire by about 30% in general staffing and about 40% in specialized staffing over 18 months, with own sourcing at 31% of gross joinees in Q2 vs 28% in Q1.

rows.label: Capital deployment of net free cash
rows.why: Net free cash is INR350 crore after the INR238 crore buyback, and an M&A framework is in place, but no ticket size, target or timeline has been disclosed.

rows.label: Receivables and OCF normalisation
rows.why: H1 OCF was negative because of about INR120 crore of one-day ad hoc funding around the EPFO wage ceiling change (recovered next day), with receivables at INR630 crore vs INR540 crore and DSO held at 6 days.
